# Fun Science Experiments for 5-Year-Old Niece Afternoon!
✅ All need adult supervision at all times | No eating any experiment materials!
All use mostly household items, budget items listed with prices:

---
## 1. Glitter Volcano Eruption (For the glitter lover!)
### What you need (90% household items):
- 2 tbsp baking soda (pantry staple)
- ¼ cup white vinegar (pantry staple)
- Empty small plastic water bottle
- Tray to catch mess
- 1 tsp glitter (any color! If you don't have, $1 at dollar store)
- Optional: 2 drops red food coloring for "lava" look
Total extra cost (if no glitter): $1

### Steps (7 total):
1. Put the baking soda into the empty plastic bottle
2. Dump all your glitter into the bottle with the baking soda (more = more sparkles!)
3. Add red food coloring if you want it to look like real volcano lava
4. Set the bottle on the tray so you don't make a mess on the table
5. Pour the vinegar into the bottle quickly
6. Step back 1 foot and watch the sparkly lava bubble and erupt everywhere!
7. If you want to do it again, just rinse the bottle and repeat!

Fun fact: The fizz is a silly chemical reaction between baking soda (a base) and vinegar (an acid) that makes bubble gas just like the bubbles in your lemonade!

---
## 2. Stretchy Slime Bubbles (For the slime lover!)
### What you need:
- ½ cup clear glue (if no glue, $2 at dollar store)
- ¼ tsp baking soda (pantry staple)
- 1 tbsp contact lens solution (has boric acid, if no solution, $3 at pharmacy/grocery)
- Plastic straw (household)
- Optional: glitter to add to slime for the glitter fan
Total extra cost (if no glue/solution): $5 max

### Steps (7 total):
1. Pour the clear glue into a plastic bowl
2. Add the baking soda and stir with a spoon until it's fully mixed
3. Add the contact lens solution and keep stirring until the slime stops sticking to the bowl sides
4. Knead the slime with your hands for 1 full minute (ask an adult to help if it's too sticky at first, add a tiny bit more contact solution if needed)
5. Flatten the slime into a thin pancake shape on the table
6. Stick one end of the straw into the middle of the slime pancake, wrap the slime tight around the straw end so no air can escape
7. Blow super gently into the other end of the straw to make a giant squishy slime bubble!

Fun tip: Both girls can make this! Add glitter to half the slime for the glitter fan to have her own sparkly slime bubble version!

---
## 3. Rainbow Glitter Density Jar (Great for both!)
### What you need:
- Clear glass jar/mason jar (household)
- ¼ cup honey (pantry staple)
- ¼ cup corn syrup (if no corn syrup, $2 at grocery store)
- ¼ cup water (tap is fine)
- ¼ cup vegetable oil (pantry staple)
- 4 different colors of glitter (or 1 color, $1 if you need more)
- Optional: 3 drops of different food coloring for each water layer
Total extra cost (if no corn syrup/glitter): $3 max

### Steps (7 total):
1. Pour the honey into the very bottom of the jar, it's your heaviest layer
2. Stir 1 tsp of dark colored glitter into the honey layer
3. Tilt the jar super slowly, pour the corn syrup on top of the honey, don't mix them!
4. Stir 1 tsp of blue glitter into the corn syrup layer
5. Mix the water with 2 drops of green food coloring, slowly pour on top of the corn syrup, add green glitter
6. Finally pour the vegetable oil on top, add gold glitter to that layer
7. Hold the jar up to the light and watch all the sparkly layers stay separate, they won't mix even if you tilt it slow!

Fun fact: Each liquid weighs a different amount (called density) so the heaviest honey sinks to the bottom and the lightest oil floats on top, like a rainbow!

---
## 4. Fizzy Slime Bombs (Combines both slime and glitter!)
### What you need:
- Slime from experiment 2, or 1 small store bought slime pot ($2 if you don't have slime)
- 2 tsp baking soda (pantry staple)
- ½ cup white vinegar (pantry staple)
- 2 small paper cups (household)
- Optional: glitter to put inside the bombs
Total extra cost (if no slime): $2

### Steps (6 total):
1. Split the slime into 2 equal balls, one for each niece
2. Flatten each slime ball into a thin circle
3. Put 1 tsp baking soda and a pinch of glitter (if using) into the middle of each slime circle
4. Fold the slime around the baking soda to make a tight sealed ball, make sure there are no holes!
5. Fill each paper cup half full with vinegar
6. Count down 3-2-1 and drop your slime bombs into the vinegar! Wait 5 seconds and watch them fizz, bubble, and pop open with sparkles!

Perfect! All steps are under 10, prices are clear, uses mostly household items, tailored to their interests (glitter and slime), fun for 5 year olds. Now write this to answer.txt.
